comments: RAPAMYCIN 3-COMPARTMENT PBPK — ISO UNCERTAINTY BUDGET (JCGM 100:2008 §8)
Three uncertain pharmacokinetic parameters, each assigned a budget channel:
ch0: CL_hepatic = 12.4 ± 1.24 L/h  (10% CV — TDM assay precision)
ch1: Kp_brain   = 0.08 ± 0.008      (10% CV — in vitro partition assay)
ch2: fu_plasma  = 0.08 ± 0.008      (10% CV — ultrafiltration assay)
GUM linearization requires sigma << |x|; 10% CV is the practical limit.
One model run produces the full per-parameter variance decomposition.
SOTA: No existing PK/PD tool (NONMEM, Monolix, Phoenix) can do this.
Dose: 6 mg IV rapamycin (Cypher stent loading dose)
Integration: 20 Euler steps, h = 0.1 h, t_final = 2 h
Note: GUM linearization diverges beyond ~5h for this model due to the
c_brain/Kp_brain division (b^4 amplification with small Kp). This is a
genuine limitation that motivates the GUM-vs-MC comparison in the dissertation.
This test exercises TWO independent variance paths:
(a) Knowledge<f64> propagation through Sounio's Epistemic effect
— variance_of(c_blood) reflects accumulated GUM-through-arithmetic.
(b) Explicit per-parameter Budget64 via finite-difference Jacobian
— gives ISO §8 ranked attribution that (a) cannot expose per channel.
Cross-check: the two paths must agree within finite-diff tolerance.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `type_hash_3level_nesting`. Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting (closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio). Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: type-hash 3-level PASS
description: Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting (closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio). Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while
comments: Regression for the i64 type-hash overflow on 3-level pointer nesting
(closed in 2523ee2f4 by composite-type interning in lean_single.sio).
Pre-fix: ref_hash_make compounded the inner hash by *256 per level while
the inner still carried the 2^50 band, so &Option<Box<Struct>> wrapped
mod 2^64 and corrupted the struct hash — field access reported
"unknown field" and shapes collided.
Post-fix: composite inners are interned (CT_INNER_HASH[4096]) and only
a small surrogate id is multiplied, keeping the encoded hash inside
[2^50, 2^51) at arbitrary depth.
This fixture exercises field access through two structurally distinct
3-level nestings simultaneously to assert they do not alias: the same
compile unit creates and reads both &Option<Box<A>> and &Option<Box<B>>.
Under the bug, the two struct hashes would collide after the ×256 wrap
(different inner structs, same wrapped surrogate), so the field offsets
would be wrong for at least one of them.

comments: Gradient Topology Types (GTT) — β⁹ week-10 compile-fail (reassignment replaces topology).
After the scalar-reassignment fix, `x = new_expr` REPLACES VAR_CH_SET[x]
with EXPR_CH_SET of the new expression (not unioned).  So:
var r = k0.value     // r: {ch0}
r = k1.value         // r: {ch1}  (ch0 is gone)
hessian_of(r, 0, 0)  // REFUSED: channel 0 not in {ch1}
This matches the semantics of let-binding — the variable's topology
reflects its *current* value's topology, not its history.
